Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings: 38-year-old female with 3 days of profuse watery→loose diarrhoea (≥4 BMs today), repeated vomiting (unable to retain fluids), subjective fever, periumbilical cramping pain, recent close contact (brother) with identical illness. No blood in stool/urine, no rash. Hydration still adequate enough to void urine 1 h prior.  
- Working diagnosis: Acute infectious gastroenteritis, most likely viral (norovirus) given household cluster and typical presentation.  
- Supporting DDx:  
  • Acute viral gastroenteritis – High likelihood (sudden onset, family cluster, vomiting, watery diarrhoea, low-grade fever, no blood).  
  • Acute bacterial gastroenteritis – Medium likelihood (persistent >72 h, subjective high fever; stool culture warranted).  
- Management:  
  • Continue oral rehydration solution, small frequent sips.  
  • Dietary advice: bland foods (toast, biscuits); avoid milk, fruit/vegetables until settled.  
  • Arrange urgent in-clinic appointment for hydration assessment and stool sample for culture and viral PCR.  
  • Safety-net: attend ED if worsening, unable to urinate, persistent vomiting, or signs of severe dehydration.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Acute viral gastroenteritis (High) – Classic presentation with family cluster, abrupt onset watery diarrhoea, vomiting, and low-grade fever; no blood in stool.  
2. Acute bacterial gastroenteritis (Medium) – Persistent symptoms beyond 72 h and subjective high fever; requires stool culture to rule out Campylobacter/Salmonella/E. coli.
